jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: The Luxury Apartment
jokes.joke: My landlord calls my apartment a luxury residence. The ceiling leaks, the windows don't close, and the mice have stopped running when I turn on the lights. One of them actually looked annoyed. I complained to my landlord, and he said, 'You're paying for the location.' I said, 'What location? I'm indoors, and somehow I'm still exposed to the elements.'

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Estimate
jokes.joke: My mechanic is the most condescending man I've ever met. I brought my car in and he looked under the hood and sighed like a doctor delivering bad news to a smoker. He said, 'Who's been doing your oil changes?' I said, 'Me.' He said, 'Ah.' Then he charged me $400 for the 'Ah.' It's itemized. Right there on the bill: 'Ah. Labor.'

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Load-Bearing
jokes.joke: I tried to be playful and surprise my girlfriend by hiding in the closet of my incredibly run-down apartment. When she walked in, I kicked the door open and yelled, 'Boo!' She didn't scream. She didn't laugh. She just slumped in relief and said, 'Oh, thank god. I thought the load-bearing raccoons had finally breached the drywall.'

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Industrial Chic
jokes.joke: I live in a run-down apartment, but I still act haughty about it. When friends visit I give the full tour. 'Notice the exposed brick—or as I call it, the wall that simply gave up. And the kitchen is fully equipped, provided you count the toaster that only works when you threaten it.'

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Maintenance Request
jokes.joke: I live in such a run-down apartment that when the sink started making a grinding noise, the landlord didn't send a plumber, he sent a mechanic. The guy listened under the faucet, nodded, and said, 'Good news, your transmission is fine. Bad news, your kitchen has 180,000 miles on it.'

scores.comment: Strong observational premise, natural escalation, and a satisfying final punchline. 'Ah. Labor.' is a concise, memorable payoff that makes the mechanic's condescension tangible.
The girlfriend's unexpected relief provides a genuine reversal. 'Load-bearing raccoons' is a funny visual, but the elaborate final sentence sounds more written than spoken, weakening the delivery.
Clear premise and consistent characterization, but the jokes about exposed brick and threatening appliances are familiar. The closing line is mildly amusing rather than a strong comedic turn.
Clean setup, natural misdirection, and efficient escalation. The transmission diagnosis sets up the apartment mileage punchline effectively. A strong, accessible joke with good stage rhythm.
Solid landlord-spin setup, and 'indoors, still exposed to the elements' is a clean closer. The 'annoyed mouse' beat is the freshest image. Familiar territory, but well built.

The reversal, where she's relieved it's only her boyfriend and not a raccoon, is a real turn. 'Load-bearing raccoons' is a vivid, odd image that lands. The setup is a bit wordy, and 'playful' is stated outright rather than shown.

The haughty-tour framing is a workable premise. 'The wall that simply gave up' and the threatened toaster are decent but predictable. Ends on a good line, though the premise is stated up front rather than discovered.

The landlord sending a mechanic for a sink is a clever absurd premise. The mileage closer is tight and carries the laugh. The transmission wordplay is a bit pun-adjacent, but the structure is clean and economical.
Competent but relies on familiar bad-apartment tropes; the punchline is a bit wordy and lacks a strong snap.
Excellent stage rhythm and pacing. The comparison to a doctor is vivid, and the itemized 'Ah. Labor' is a very strong, relatable punchline.
The opening sentence is pure, unnatural prompt recitation, which ruins the stage illusion. The subsequent observations feel disjointed.
Uses a slightly dated setup structure, but pays it off nicely with a clean, well-escalated absurd premise. The final line lands solidly.
Solid apartment complaint with a mild location turn; competent but forgettable.
Clean premise, sharp non-obvious billable 'Ah' that carries the laugh.
Playful setup lands on a fresh, specific raccoon image with good relief snap.
Economical car/house swap; mild and familiar payoff.
Clear premise and voice; indoor-yet-exposed line is amusing, but the turn is fairly predictable and modest.
Strong character detail, efficient buildup, and the itemized 'Ah. Labor.' tag is a solid, clean punchline.
Good misdirection and escalation; 'load-bearing raccoons' is vivid and the reveal delivers a strong laugh.
Fun contrast between pride and decay; contains good lines, but feels more like a string of observations than a sharpened punch.
